Residential Pressure Washing in Dallas-Fort Worth

Patios, front walks, pool decks, porches and steps: the hard surfaces around a North Texas home. Call the free line and you are put through to a local company that sizes the pressure to each one.

Residential pressure washing covers the hard ground around a house: the patio you sit on, the walk to the front door, the pool deck, porch steps and stone borders. In Dallas-Fort Worth those surfaces collect oak pollen in spring, clay dust in summer and black mildew wherever shade lingers. A proper cleaning removes it evenly without scarring the surface.

This line does not clean anything. It is a free phone number that connects you with a company that does. You call, an automated assistant asks what you need and how big the area is, and you are transferred to an independent, locally owned DFW pressure washing company. That company quotes the work, books a time with you, does the job and is paid by you.

Surface by surface: what a good company changes

"Pressure washing" is really a set of methods. The right one depends on what the surface is made of. Here is how the common surfaces around a Texas home are usually handled.

How common home surfaces are usually cleaned
SurfaceUsual approachWhat to watch for
Broom-finish concrete patio or walkRotary surface cleaner across the flat area, wand on edges and stepsStripes from a narrow wand swept back and forth
Pool deck coatingLower pressure and a cleaner suited to the coatingPeeling a textured or painted coating; runoff into the pool
Flagstone, pavers, stamped concreteModerate pressure, then re-sanding joints if neededBlowing out joint sand or lifting loose stones
Brick steps and bordersLow pressure and a masonry-safe cleaner, test spot firstEroded mortar joints and chipped brick faces
Painted porch floorGentle wash, often as paint prepLifting paint that was ready to fail anyway

The Brick Industry Association's guidance on cleaning brickwork says high-pressure water cleaning is not appropriate for brick and recommends trying a small test area first and letting it dry before judging the result. That habit, a test patch before the whole job, is a good sign in any company.

Why North Texas concrete gets dirty fast

Much of DFW sits on expansive black clay that swells when it is wet and shrinks when it dries. The Dallas County Master Gardeners describe that clay contracting and cracking in summer drought, and swelling, even heaving, when it is soaked. Patios and walks ride those movements, so they develop hairline cracks and slight lips at the joints, and every crack holds dirt and moisture.

Add oak pollen in spring, which NBC 5's weather team describes as the yellow dust that coats homes and patios, plus sprinkler overspray and summer heat that bakes grime on, and a light-colored slab can look gray within a year or two.

When you might need pressure washing near you

  • Before selling or listing a home. Clean walks and patios show up in every listing photo.
  • Before painting or staining. Paint makers say to wash first; Sherwin-Williams suggests letting the surface dry 24 to 48 hours before painting.
  • After a storm. Spring hail and wind leave grit, shredded leaves and mud splashed across hardscape.
  • When a walk turns slick. Green growth on shaded concrete can make steps slippery when wet.
  • Ahead of an HOA inspection. Many neighborhood associations send notices for stained walks and drives. Check your deed restrictions for what they require.

Not sure what the surface needs? Call and describe it. The company you are connected with can tell you how it would clean it and what it would charge.

The real dangers of pressure washing a home

Most of the harm comes from pressure used where it does not belong. Water forced under lap siding or around window frames can soak insulation and framing. Mortar joints on brick can wash out. Wood gets furry and gouged. Shingles lose their granules. And on the safety side, ladders, wet surfaces and a wand that kicks back are a poor mix for someone doing it for the first time. That is the case for calling a company that does this every week and can show proof of insurance.

Before washing, a good company will also ask what you have used on the surface before. Sealers, paints and old stain treatments change what cleaner is safe to use.

Where the rinse water goes

Storm drains in North Texas are not treated. The regional council of governments' stormwater FAQ notes that no local government in North Central Texas treats stormwater, so whatever goes down the curb inlet reaches the nearest creek.

The City of Dallas tells property owners that wash water may only go to the street or storm drain if it is plain water with no soap, degreaser or other chemical, does not harm the creek, and does not cause erosion or muddy runoff. If cleaning chemicals are used, Dallas says to block the storm drain and collect the contaminated water. Ask the company how it handles runoff on your street.

What the visit usually looks like

  1. Walk-around and quoteThe company looks at each surface, points out stains, cracks and loose pavers, and prices each item.
  2. PrepPlants near the work are wet down or covered, outlets and fixtures protected, drains blocked if needed.
  3. Pre-treatmentMildew, rust or oil spots get the right cleaner first, given time to work.
  4. WashFlat concrete with a surface cleaner, edges and steps with a wand at the right distance.
  5. Rinse and walk-throughGrime is rinsed off the walk and beds, and you check the result together.

Common questions

What does residential pressure washing include?

It usually means the hard outdoor surfaces of a home: concrete and stone patios, front walks, pool decks, porches, steps, retaining walls and sometimes the driveway. Siding, roofs and wood are normally handled as separate items because they need low pressure. Ask the company to list each surface on the quote so you know exactly what is covered.

Is pressure washing dangerous for my house?

It can be when it is aimed at the wrong thing. High pressure can strip mortar from brick joints, which the Brick Industry Association warns about, drive water behind siding and window frames, and damage asphalt shingles, which the roofing manufacturers say should never be power washed. On bare concrete it is the right tool. A careful company changes method by surface.

What should I do before the pressure washing company arrives?

Move cars, patio furniture, grills and planters off the area, close windows and doors, and pick up toys and hoses. Point out outdoor outlets, light fixtures, cracked concrete and anything fragile. Make sure the company can reach an outdoor faucet, and mention if you are on a watering day restriction so it can plan.

Can a pool deck be pressure washed with water in the pool?

Yes, a company does this all the time, but the dirty rinse water and any cleaning solution should not run into the pool. Ask how it will keep runoff out, and whether a cool, textured or painted deck coating needs a gentler approach than bare concrete.

Do I need to be home while my patio is pressure washed?

Usually not for outdoor-only work, as long as the company can reach the water spigot and the gate. That is between you and the company. Agree on access, the price and what will be cleaned before the visit.
